ev.q: In 2015, an estimated 1.3% (1.2% age-adjusted) of U.S. adults (3.1 million) had ever received a diagnosis of IBD
A higher percentage of adults aged 45–64 (1.5%) and ≥65 (1.7%) years had IBD
In 2015, an estimated 3.1 million (1.3%) of U.S. adults had ever received a diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease
Hispanics (1.2%) and non-Hispanic whites (1.4%) had a higher prevalence of IBD than did non-Hispanic blacks (0.5%).
Comparisons among subgroups used age-adjusted estimates of IBD prevalence, which were calculated using the projected 2000 U.S. population as the standard population
NHIS is a household survey that provides nationally representative estimates on a broad range of health measures

methods_quotes.q: Comparisons among subgroups used age-adjusted estimates of IBD prevalence, which were calculated using the projected 2000 U.S. population as the standard population
Sampling weights were used for all estimates, and the complex sample design of the NHIS was accounted for by using SUDAAN 11.0 software
For comparisons of prevalence between subgroups, statistical significance (p<0.05) was determined by two-tailed Z-tests.
The National Center for Health Statistics’ standard for reliability is for an estimate to have a relative standard error <30.0%
